newsitem.title: USA: Calif runoff forecast high, but reduced by dry Feb.
newsitem.headline: Calif runoff forecast high, but reduced by dry Feb.

text.p: California's April to July runoff is still forecast above normal at 125 percent of average levels, despite a dry February, the state's Department of Water Resources said Tuesday in its latest forecast update.
The runoff estimate gives an indication of the state's capacity for generating hydroelectric power, which can account for as much as 40 percent of total power output in a wet year.
Runoff for the water year as a whole (Oct 1, 1996 to Sep 30, 1997) is forecast to average 170 percent of normal because of heavy flooding this winter.
Spring runoff on the San Joaquin River in the southern Sierra mountains was forecast at 145 percent of normal, compared with an early-February forecast of 180 percent.
Snowpack water content is about 115 percent of average statewide, and much higher than that in the southern Sierras, the state agency said.
Runoff so far this season was 230 percent of average, nearly double the 120 percent seen last year.
Reservoir storage was assessed at 120 percent of average, with actual volume down 2.4 million acre feet from early February because of efforts to clear space for flood control.
